reading.body:
Anna Hegreness is named on 13 AI lobbying filings, all filed through one firm, all for a single client, Google Client Services LLC, and all naming bills from 2025 or later.

The pattern is concentration on two axes. One lobbyist, one firm, one client, and 26 distinct bills. The filings do not spread across a roster of companies. They run through a single corporate client and reach a wide set of legislation, which is what a dedicated government affairs operation looks like in disclosure data rather than what a broad industry coalition looks like.

For AI specifically, this is the policy layer that sits between compute buildout and the rules that govern it. Data centers, power contracts, and model deployment all depend on statutes and appropriations that these bills would set. A client with the resources to track 26 bills at once is buying coverage of that surface, not a single issue.

What the data does not say is what any of these bills contain, whether they passed, or what position the client took. It records that a name appears on filings, nothing about influence or outcome. It also covers only AI-tagged filings held by this site, so it is a slice of a lobbying record, not the whole of it.
